claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 3.0, annual return 10%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 3.03 to 3.07 (change +0.04).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 3.03 to 3.03. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.96 (as submitted, 5 bps: 3.03); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 3.03 against 3.03 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 3.38 against 3.03 in research, a gap of -0.35.
The best year gives 17% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give 93%; Sharpe is 3.96 in calm and 0.83 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 3.00 becomes 3.00 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 3.14 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.01, 95th percentile 0.53).
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 20% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 20% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
